parsed.attack: StudyBlue is the clearest entry in the flashcard graveyard: Chegg paid $20.8 million for it in 2018, discontinued it at the end of 2020 in favour of a free successor, and shut that free successor in 2022 - a product with millions of users could not be made to pay, because the card content is the commodity and free code decks already sit on Anki and Quizlet. Habitual [63] supplies the other half: in a category of hundreds of near-identical entrants the channel decides survival, and the channel named here - instructors and journeymen recommending it - is asserted rather than unlocked, in a market where Mike Holt already owns that relationship and sells multi-hundred-dollar packages through it. Nothing in flat-priced long context changes either fact; the fourth kill criterion tests the inference bill, which was never what killed anything in this category.
parsed.strongest_defence: A booked licensing exam supplies an acuteness and a deadline that StudyBlue's undifferentiated student market never had, and $29 once against a licence worth tens of thousands a year is not a consumer-subscription decision at all.
parsed.verdict_reason: The dated exam is a real difference from StudyBlue's market, but the commodity-content and no-channel causes that closed StudyBlue and Habitual are untouched by cheaper context.
